analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The patch (head lines 1751-1753) adds three table rows listing environment variables forwarded into the launchd daemon: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. They point to GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift and EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift. The supplied units are base_text excerpts (lines 1-830) that do not contain the changed region, so I could not see the table's surrounding context or the source behavior behind these variables. This is documentation-only; no executable code, auth, attestation, crypto, or coordinator protocol change is visible.

Threat-model relevance: the new variables concern KV cache retention, idle cache sweep and segment host-zeroing. These touch T-028 (residual inference data in GPU/host memory) and T-041 (prefix-cache storage), but the supplied evidence shows only that the env keys are forwarded into launchd, not what they do. Unverified contract: if DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION or DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS retain KV segments beyond request completion, or disable zeroing, residual-data exposure (T-028) could change. Likewise, if the operator-supplied values widen cache reuse, T-041 could be affected. The source files were not supplied, so I cannot confirm that. Integration should check that these knobs cannot widen cross-tenant cache reuse or weaken zeroing, and that the threat model does not need an update. No concrete security regression is established from the evidence provided, so there are no findings. I set needs_deeper_review=true only because of that missing implementation evidence and the unseen changed region.
